pr_title: Display performance breakdown in a tooltip
pr_body:
Closes #15570 

~Depends on #16575 for correct breakdown values~ No longer the case

~Add a tooltip to `PerformanceStatistic` displaying pp breakdown.~ See updates below

<details>
<summary>Old screenshot</summary>

![osu! 17_1_2022 9_26_01 pm (2)](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/25472513/149779639-6df4650e-6f31-49f9-a898-273db7f77c41.png)

</details>


# Updates

Here's a summary of major changes since the initial commit so reviewers/newcomers don't have to scroll through the entire conversation:

- Instead of showing the absolute attribute values, a perfect play is created based on the beatmap, ruleset, and mods selected, then the achieved performance is compared with the perfect play performance to generate a percentage for each attribute.
- Currently, this comparison assumes that attribute values are combined linearly to generate the final PP value, which is a close approximation, but not exactly the case. However, correcting for this non-linear combination requires refactoring the performance calculator, which is not included in this PR.
- The entire chart has been moved from a tooltip to the expanded results screen for better visibility. The expanded results screen has been refactored to support items like this one that don't require watching a replay to display.
- The performance breakdown revealed that osu diffcalc doesn't properly support lazer-first scores (at least in terms of max combo calculation). A local function has been added in `PerformanceBreakdownCalculator` to circumvent this. The fix to osu diffcalc is tracked in #16575.

<details>
<summary>Screenshots</summary>

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/25472513/152666640-7d09668e-1b61-4438-a785-39e2af9161f7.png)

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/25472513/152666658-2686a23c-bb3d-4f4d-aab5-b12a5e286992.png)

</details>
pr_comments: holy you are fast, looks rather primitive but def works

The numbers make no sense though? The way this tooltip is structured suggests that the values next to the bars should total to the sum. But they don't, even on the screenshot above 71+36+90 sums up to 197 and not 202. And that's because the constituent parts are combined in a non-linear manner to the final pp.

Like the raw performance attribute values don't matter to anyone besides maybe pp developers, because they're *not actual pp points* - so why show them?

The way the bars are linearly scaled to the sum of the attributes is also questionable. There's no standardisation in place that says that the attributes must be even anywhere near the same magnitude.

> The numbers make no sense though? The way this tooltip is structured suggests that the values next to the bars should total to the sum. But they don't, even on the screenshot above 71+36+90 sums up to 197 and not 202. And that's because the constituent parts are combined in a non-linear manner to the final pp.
> 
> Like the raw performance attribute values don't matter to anyone besides maybe pp developers, because they're _not actual pp points_ - so why show them?
> 
> The way the bars are linearly scaled to the sum of the attributes is also questionable. There's no standardisation in place that says that the attributes must be even anywhere near the same magnitude.

because people have  been wanting to see the constituent parts of PP forever, to tell at a glance what a plays strongest areas are, simple as

...except for the part where this isn't the actual breakdown of a performance? precisely because the attributes are combined into the final value in a non-trivial manner? the bar graph is actively misleading. it makes you think the final pp value is the sum of the breakdown parts. while it may be nowhere near.

here's a taiko example:

![osu_2022-01-17_15-45-22](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/20418176/149790532-e59c7252-d8a7-4547-b366-b0848d01cf6c.jpg)

and a particularly egregious mania example:

![osu_2022-01-17_15-42-18](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/20418176/149790567-41d00da5-b4b4-40ec-ade2-41a6ea10b8a4.jpg)

the fact that a feature is oft-requested does not mean that it has to be implemented by all costs when it's not really functioning as expected. taking raw performance values and just chucking them into a bar graph is not the correct way to proceed.

What would make sense for having these is when comparing them against a perfect play, as already mentioned in https://github.com/ppy/osu/discussions/15566#discussioncomment-1623891, instead of what seems to be just an arbitrary width to the bar. And also not consider the final PP value as the direct "Total" as mentioned above.

i agree the above sounds workable. i'd imagine that would work in the following way:

take the score's performance attributes, compute performance attributes for a perfect play, and then for each performance attribute value from the user's score fix other attributes to the perfect value and then calculate the pp for that "mixed" score. the amount of pp lost on this skill relative to the perfect play would work in a way for a breakdown.

even then i probably wouldn't show raw numbers because they're likely to also make no sense. maybe each attribute could be ranked by percentage or something, or have a letter rank attached.
Percentage is what I would have proposed.

The bar chart is now changed to compare performance attributes to a perfect play:

![osu! 18_1_2022 10_13_35 pm](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/25472513/149953695-736facaa-2285-4f6c-81d1-430e1f2860b4.png)

To avoid misconceptions, this breakdown only shows you how a score could be improved when compared to a perfect play of the same map. An SS play would simply have 100% across the board because it _is_ a perfect play. Visualizing star rating attributes (#9463) should give you a better understanding of the skills demonstrated in a play.
Will this work for all rulesets?
Yes, except catch which doesn't have separate attributes in the performance calculator

I've merged `master` here for ease of review, to not have to juggle back and forth from sqlite to realm. Seems pretty safe now that there is a backup procedure in place.

@Henry-YSLin just a heads up - if you try to run this now then you'll have your database migrated. I think it's generally best that as many devs try to run this early as possible before next release so that we can fix up any errors that transpire. If you're very worried about losing data you may also use the "second client" run config.

I've tested this some more and I'm generally okay with this I think, but I would still like to get a second fresh opinion from someone who hasn't seen this diff this many times yet.

There's one breakage - in playlists, sometimes score panels are used even when the beatmap isn't locally available, but the current checks for that don't quite work and therefore the tooltip still shows with some rather nonsensical results:

![osu_2022-01-22_14-43-53](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/20418176/150640896-1e6f01f1-5b9d-43f9-bc09-81d71273531e.jpg)

but the underlying general issue there is #16480 and therefore fixing this here is probably out of scope...?

Found a pretty serious problem with the performance breakdown calculation. The breakdown is completely inaccurate for a score set without classic mod in the osu ruleset. From the screenshot below, it is clear that the score should have perfect performance, but the performance breakdown just outputs bogus values.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/25472513/150644177-36a10bdd-07d4-4d1f-81af-861bd6fc8c03.png)

I have a rough idea why this is happening, but I haven't got time to fix it right now. Gonna set this PR to draft for now to prevent premature merging.

It's probably due to combo scaling. Classic mod being enabled influences possible max combo.

Also not strictly necessary to mark as draft, I could have added a "blocked" tag on this. But I guess either works.
Just going to mention that the "x/y" display next to final pp is hard to understand. I can't even imagine what it's intending to convey.

> I can't even imagine what it's intending to convey.

The maximum achievable PP. Perhaps you're confused because the screenshot was taken without the existence of the classic mod, and diffcalc doesn't currently support lazer-first scores (see: https://github.com/ppy/osu/pull/16575). It would be 198/198 for a perfect score as in the screenshot with that fixed.

Wow okay. Maybe I'm just stupid.

But I also wouldn't display it like that. The maximum should be its own row, or in parenthesis or something. As a fraction reads really badly IMHO (we don't do that anywhere else for PP which is likely why I was confused).

Does this look better? I have to remove the bar in the middle, otherwise it looks odd being stuck between 2 lines.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/25472513/151975651-e24f25d0-3842-4d9c-8373-f7f4fd1e0eb9.png)
I think it's okay. Someone may be able to come up with better terminology for the text.

> Does this look better? I have to remove the bar in the middle, otherwise it looks odd being stuck between 2 lines.
> 
> ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/25472513/151975651-e24f25d0-3842-4d9c-8373-f7f4fd1e0eb9.png)
> 

Imo achieved PP sounds better than final PP and juxtaposes itself better with maximum PP

> Does this look better? I have to remove the bar in the middle, otherwise it looks odd being stuck between 2 lines.
> 
> ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/25472513/151975651-e24f25d0-3842-4d9c-8373-f7f4fd1e0eb9.png)

I don't know if this is possible or a good idea, but I think plays without the Flashlight mod applied (which is like the majority of plays) should just have the bar and the percentage on the "Flashlight Bonus" row be replaced with the text "Flashlight not applied" or something similar.

> I don't know if this is possible or a good idea, but I think plays without the Flashlight mod applied (which is like the majority of plays) should just have the bar and the percentage on the "Flashlight Bonus" row be replaced with the text "Flashlight not applied" or something similar.

You could just not show a skill on the graph if the perfect play with the given beatmap and mods receives nothing pp-wise from that given skill. Assuming non-FL plays universally get 0 FL bonus this would have the desired effect.
Agree with hiding zero values.

This may be an unwanted drive-by comment, but is there a reason this extra info is being implemented as a tooltip rather than on the expanded score and statistics display that shows when you click on a score card? It seems like a more logical place to put this kind of info?

Also agree that it is best moved to the expanded results screen. Displaying this kind of information in a tooltip is obtuse and hidden, and we added the expanded screen specifically for statistics like this.

> Agree with hiding zero values.

Alright, will do.

> Also agree that it is best moved to the expanded results screen.

I reckon that would be the ideal place too, but currently the expanded results screen requires you to watch the replay before showing the stats, while pp breakdown doesn't really require the replay to calculate. Wouldn't it be too annoying to require users to do extra useless work before seeing the breakdown?

The requirement for watching replay can be moved locally to the components which require it. Note that if this path is to be taken and it's more than a few lines of change, it should be done in a separate pull request to this one.

The entire chart has been moved to the expanded results screen:

<details>
<summary>Screenshots</summary>

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/25472513/152666640-7d09668e-1b61-4438-a785-39e2af9161f7.png)

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/25472513/152666658-2686a23c-bb3d-4f4d-aab5-b12a5e286992.png)

</details>

Also, in an effort to unblock this PR, I added a function to calculate beatmap max combo locally in `PerformanceBreakdownCalculator`. It is essentially the same function as in #16575, which allows the effect of classic mod to be properly considered. As a result, the breakdown chart now displays results as expected (autoplay gets all 100%, no more above-100% weirdness).

Although the absolute PP value is still inaccurate (that would have to rely on #16575 to be fixed), the value on the chart matches those displayed in other places (e.g. performance statistic in the score panel), so it should be fine to go ahead with this PR for now. Gonna mark this as ready for review.
I think this seems fine for an initial effort. It's ugly, but so are the other statistics displays. I figure we'll do a design pass on all these in a grouped effort in the future.

issue_context.title: Display a breakdown of the user's PP in the results screen
issue_context.body:
### Discussed in https://github.com/ppy/osu/discussions/15566
Originally posted by **developomp** November 11, 2021 Show breakdown of pp (aim, speed, accuracy, etc.) in the result screen.
comments: I would like to try implementing this. How about a tooltip on the "PP" statistic item?

> I would like to try implementing this. How about a tooltip on the "PP" statistic item?

do you have sort of like an idea of what the visuals will be like for such a feature?

i think a spider web chart or bar chart would be the ideal presentation for this, text alone would lack the quick digestibility

Spider web charts won't work for taiko and mania because they only have 2 pp attributes (accuracy and difficulty)

Bar charts might work, but we need to figure out a maximum value to scale the attributes to. Using total pp as maximum won't work because it is affected by multipliers and may be smaller than attribute values.

> Spider web charts won't work for taiko and mania because they only have 2 pp attributes (accuracy and difficulty)
> 
> Bar charts might work, but we need to figure out a maximum value to scale the attributes to. Using total pp as maximum won't work because it is affected by multipliers and may be smaller than attribute values.

yeah  good point about mania and taiko,

why wouldnt the sum of the bars being the total pp not work? 

simply scale the pp bar size down to a fixed size so they dont change in total size among different total pp values no?

By "total pp" I meant the final value you see in the results screen.

But yeah a simple sum should work. Lemme work on it a bit and see

review_comments: I haven't managed to get this spinner to ever appear so it's hard to test whether it displays correctly or not. Were you manually adding delays to test this out?
Yep. It is working fine. The chart is taller than the spinner, causing a height change when it finishes loading, but I guess it's not noticeable anyway.

Could make this a `Component`, at which point you could  use DI the same way as you would from a standard drawable, so long as the calculator is `Add()`ed to another composite drawable. Maybe not necesssary though.
Probably not necessary. Feels weird to add a calculator to draw hierarchy just for DI.
Feels like this should maybe be moved to `LoadComplete` to avoid potentially calculating before the user requests details statistics. But I guess it's fine as-is until we notice an issue.
In my testing, it only starts calculation when the detailed statistics panel is first shown, so it should be fine.

Not sure about this change. This way every score PP calculation will store a copy of the "perfect play" attribute values. So there'll be N copies of the same data for N user scores, and each copy will be calculated from scratch. Seems kinda wasteful.

Would you prefer a separate cache for perfect play performance or computing it on the fly without caching? I don't think a cache is necessary but I could be wrong seeing that `ScorePerformanceCache` is created with `PerformanceStatistic` being its only usage.

Update: Changed performance breakdown calculator to calculate perfect performance without caching.

Caching would be optimal (because you'd only have to cache one per difficulty) but upon checking it seems to be not-horrible performance wise even on marathon maps like https://osu.ppy.sh/beatmapsets/29157#osu/156352 so maybe fine to keep this as is for now. Turning off perfect score pp caching is an improvement in storage at least to what was there before.
